key_insight: Pre-AF 13 is an interpretable 13-feature model that uses routine discharge report data to predict atrial fibrillation risk in cardiovascular patients over 24 months and longer follow-up.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians identify higher-risk CVD patients earlier than traditional AF risk scores, which showed weaker discrimination in this population.
method: Single-center retrospective EHR study of 17,562 cardiovascular patients without prior AF
NLP pipeline converted discharge notes into 73 structured features; LightAutoML built full, simple, and linear models
Performance was compared with CHARGE-AF, C2HEST, MHS, and HAVOC, with SHAP used for interpretability
evidence_signal: In 45,000 patients across 80,576 records, 8.19% developed AF; the simple model achieved ROC AUC 0.725 at 24 months and 0.696 over full follow-up, outperforming comparator scores.
watch_item: Results come from a single-center retrospective dataset, so external validation and prospective testing are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Pre-AF 13: An Interpretable Atrial Fibrillation Risk Score Mined from Discharge Reports
